patches.old: - **M1**: Found in the CNS and gastric parietal cells.
patches.new: - **M1**: Found in the CNS, enteric neurons and some gastric cells (e.g., chief cells; the parietal-cell acid response is mediated mainly by M3).
patches.reason: Parietal-cell acid secretion is mediated mainly by M3, not M1.

patches.old:
### Respiratory Rate

The ANS modulates respiratory rate through effects on the medullary respiratory centers. Sympathetic activation increases respiratory rate and depth during the fight-or-flight response, while parasympathetic tone predominates at rest.
patches.new:
### Respiratory Rate

Breathing rhythm is *not* set by autonomic efferents. It is generated by respiratory centers in the medulla and pons and carried to the diaphragm and intercostal muscles by **somatic** motor nerves (phrenic and intercostal). The ANS acts on the airways (caliber, mucus) rather than on the breathing muscles; the faster, deeper breathing seen in fight-or-flight comes from brainstem respiratory centers responding to the same stressors, to chemoreceptor input and to higher brain centers.
patches.reason: Respiratory rhythm comes from brainstem centers driving somatic motor nerves, not from autonomic tone.

patches.old: - Pupil constriction/miosis (M3 on ciliary muscle and sphincter pupillae)
patches.new: - Pupil constriction/miosis (M3 on the sphincter pupillae) and accommodation for near vision (M3 on the ciliary muscle)
patches.reason: Miosis is due to the sphincter pupillae; the ciliary muscle controls accommodation.

patches.old: - **Non-selective α agonists** (e.g., phenylephrine): Vasoconstriction, used as nasal decongestants and to treat hypotension.
patches.new: - **Selective α1 agonists** (e.g., phenylephrine): Vasoconstriction, used as nasal decongestants and to treat hypotension (often with reflex bradycardia).
patches.reason: Phenylephrine is a selective α1 agonist.

visual.title: One map of autonomic and somatic efferents
visual.alt: Five pathways from the CNS. Parasympathetic: long preganglionic fiber releasing ACh on nicotinic receptors at a ganglion near the organ, then a short fiber releasing ACh on muscarinic receptors. Sympathetic: short preganglionic fiber releasing ACh on nicotinic receptors, then a long fiber releasing norepinephrine on alpha or beta receptors. Sympathetic to sweat glands: same but ending with ACh on muscarinic receptors. Adrenal medulla: preganglionic ACh on nicotinic receptors of chromaffin cells, which secrete about 80 percent epinephrine plus norepinephrine into blood. Somatic: one motor neuron releasing ACh on nicotinic receptors at the neuromuscular junction.
visual.caption: Fiber lengths are schematic. Ganglionic (Nn) and muscle (Nm) nicotinic receptors are different subtypes.
